12th May, 2006]
No.PAB/Legis;V(30)/2005,
dated 12-5-2006.--The Balochistan Residential
Colleges Bill, No. 7 of 2005 having been passed by the Provincial Assembly of Balochistan on 15th April, 2006 and assented to by the
Governor of Balochisstan, is hereby published as an
Act No.VIII of 2005 the Provincial Assembly.
Preamble.--Whereas it is expedient
to provide for the establishment of the Residential Colleges in Balochistan to promote education:
It is hereby enacted as follows:--
1. Short title, extent and Commencement.---(1) This Act
may be called the Balochistan Residential Colleges
Act, 2005.
(2) It extends to the whole of the Province of Balochistan
except Tribal Areas.
(3) It shall come into force at once.

2. Definitions.----In this Act, unless the
context otherwise requires the following expressions shall have the meanings
hereby respectively assigned to them, that is to say:--
(a) "Board" means the Board of
Governors of Balochistan Residential Colleges;
(b) "Chairman" means the
Chairman of the Board;
(c) "Colleges" means the Balochistan Residential Colleges;
(d) "Controlling Authority"
means the authority as specified in section 9;
(e) "Government" means the
Government of Balochistan;
(f) "Member" means a member of
the Board;
(g) "Prescribed" means
prescribed by rules or regulations made under this Act;
(h) "Principal" means the
Principal Officer incharge
of College by whatever name called;
(i)
"Chairman and Vice-Chairman" means the Chairman and Vice-Chairman of
the Board;

4. Establishment of the Board.---(1) The
Government shall, as soon as may after the commencement of this Act, establish
a Board for all Residential Colleges to be called the Board of Governors of Balochistan Residential Colleges.
(2) The board shall be a body corporate
having perpetual succession and a common seal with powers to acquire, hold and
dispose of property, both movable and immovable and shall by the aforesaid name
sue and be sued.
Provided that the Board shall not be
competent to acquire or dispose of any immovable property without the previous
approval of the Government in writing.
(3) The head office of the Board shall be
at Quetta.
(4) The Board shall comprise of the
Chairman, Vice-Chairman and Members.

(2) The Government may remove any member

(3) Any member of the Board may, by

8. Meetings of the Board ---The meetings
of the Board shall be held in such manner and at such time as may be
prescribed:
Provided that, until rules are made in
this behalf, such meetings shall be called by the Chairman:
9. (1) Subject to the other provisions of this
Act, the Board shall have the powers to manage and control the affairs of the
College.
(2) In particular, and without prejudice
to the generality of the foregoing power, the board shall have the power.
(a) to
administer and manage the property in use of the College and the Board;
(b) to acquire
and dispose of property;
(c) to enter into
contracts in respect of the College;
(d) to appoint
the Principal, members of staff and others officers and servants of the Board
and the College on such terms and conditions as may be determined by the
Government;
(e) to formulate
the budget for the approval of the Government.
(f) to determine
the classes to be started and the number of students to be admitted in each
class annually;
(g) to lay down
procedure for admission, promotion and removal of students from college;
(h) to institute
scholarships and stipends;
(i) to set up an Executive Committee and such other Standing
Committee as may be necessary;
(j) to delegate powers to the Chairman,
Vice-Chairman, the Executive Committee, Standing Committee, the Principal, the
staff of the College and other officers of the Board.

10. Power of the Controlling Authority.---(1)
The Controlling Authority shall have power to cause an inspection to be made by
such person as it may direct, of the offices, activities and funds of, and all
examinations conducted by the Board and to cause an inquiry to be made in like
manner in respect of any matter concerning the College.
(2) The Controlling Authority shall
communicate to the Board the findings of the inspection or inquiry, and may
advise the Board to take such action and within such period as may be
specified.
(3) The Board shall report to the
Controlling Authority the action it proposes to taken on such communication.
(4) Where the board does not, within the
specified time, submit its report as required by subsection (3), or the
Controlling Authority is not satisfied with the action taken or proposed to be
taken, the Controlling Authority may, after considering any explanation given
by the Board, issue such direction as it thinks fit, and the Board shall comply
with such direction.
(5) The controlling Authority may, from
time to time, direct the board to conduct its affairs and perform its functions
in such manner as it may specify.
(6) If the Controlling Authority is
satisfied that any proceeding of the Board is not in conformity with the Act,
the Controlling Authority may, without prejudice to the foregoing provisions of
this section by an order in writing annul such proceedings:
Provided that before making any such
order to Controlling Authority shall through the Chairman, call upon the Board
to show cause as to why such an order should not be made.
(7) If the Board fails or neglects to
comply with the directives or orders given to it under subsection (5) or if, in
the opinion of the Controlling Authority, the Board persistently makes default
in the performance of its functions under this Act, the Government may
supersede the Board and appoint the Chairman in the place of such Board until a
new Board is established in accordance with the provision of this Act and no
such supersession or appointment shall be questioned
in any Court.

serving under government may be transferred by the government for service in
the colleges on such terms and conditions as Government may determine;
Provided that where a Government servant
is required to serve the colleges, his terms and conditions of service as to
his pay shall not be less favourable than those to
which he would have been entitled if he had not been so required to serve:
Provided further that
the government servant who is so required to serve shall be entitled to
deputation allowance as the Government may determine.

(3) The fund shall be utilized for

payment of salaries and other remunerations of the members, the Principal and
other members of the staff of the College and officers and servants of the

referred to as the auditor.
(2) The college shall, at the time of
audit, produce all accounts, registers, documents and other papers, which may
be required by the auditor to assist him in his investigation.
(3) The college administration shall, as
soon as possible after the end of each financial year, submit to the Government
the annual statement of account of the colleges duly audited, together with the
report of the auditor and its comments on the report.

(g) the manner

(h) any other
matter required under any of the provisions of this Act to be prescribed.
